newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cypriot fisherman gets 15 months jail in AIDS case.
newsitem.headline: Cypriot fisherman gets 15 months jail in AIDS case.

text.p: A Cyprus court on Thursday sentenced a Greek Cypriot fisherman to 15 months in jail for negligently giving the deadly virus that causes AIDS to his British lover, Janette Pink.
"This case was so severe that even the maximum penalty as provided by law is evidently inadequate," Judge Antonis Liatsos told the defendant, Pavlos Georgiou, 40.

The judge said: "He is tragically condemned and it would be expected he would have tried to avoid putting others in the same condition...without telling her, he was ejaculating death in her for months."

Georgiou, looking subdued, was immediately escorted from the court and into a police car. He did not speak to reporters but had a brief conversation with his twin brother, Petros, who was in the court.
"He has actually accepted it," the brother said of the sentence.

Georgiou, a father of four who has tested positive for the HIV virus that causes AIDS, was found guilty of repeated sexual contact with Pink, 45, from Basildon in Essex, from January 1994 until she was tested HIV positive in October 1994, without telling her of his condition.
Georgiou's youngest son is HIV positive and his wife died of an AIDS-related illness in 1994.
Charged under a decades-old law enacted to curb the spread of cholera on Cyprus, Georgiou had faced a maximum sentence of two years in jail, a 1,500 Cyprus pound ($2,770) fine, or both.
Pink did not come to Cyprus for the verdict on Tuesday at the end of a three-month trial.
Georgiou had denied Pink's accusation that he lied to her about having the disease.
Throughout the three-month hearing he had maintained Pink was well aware of his condition during their affair.

He admitted that on one occasion, when they were both drunk, they had unprotected sex. This, he said, took place after Pink, whom he described as having a "weakness" for unprotected intercourse, took the condom off him.
Shortly before the alleged incident in April 1994, Pink had taken her first AIDS test which appeared negative.

"It is inconceivable that a woman who has just found out she is healthy would have unprotected sex....it is illogical," Judge Liatsos said on Tuesday, ruling Georgiou's testimony "utterly unreliable".
Pink took a second test in October 1994, which was positive.
Pink said Georgiou lied to her about his wife's condition as well, claiming she suffered from leukaemia.
She stayed with him until July 1996, when, after developing full-blown Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome, she returned to England for medical treatment.
It was there that she decided to report Georgiou to the Cypriot authorities.
